coverage.assessment: Three of the revision's cuts weaken causal links: Carter's refusal now lacks the PM's secrecy proposal and the spies rebuttal, Carter no longer says Sir James asked him to gather facts, and the Charing Cross clue loses its explanation. The envelope and the telegram chain survive.
The entrances, the Downing Street setting, Gatehouse, Kent, and Julius's return 'from Manchester' are clear. Unattributed lines still alternate legibly between Carter and the PM.
Sir James's account becomes one unprompted monologue. Carter's nonplussed beat and his request to hear 'exactly what passed' are gone, and with them the volunteering, cautious lawyer's rhythm.

The letter loses 'That last's only a guess', and the first draft had already cut 'awful ass of myself'. Carter's 'diffident youth' rationale is also gone. 'An idea' and 'for what it's worth' keep some uncertainty.
There is no premature revelation. Sir James's insinuation and 'I know who he was' stay unexplained. Carter and the PM do not suspect Sir James. The Julius suspicion is intact.

Tommy's 'He's frightfully clever' and Carter's 'Peel Edgerton would be the man' are gone, which thins the dramatic irony. The cuts of the 'successor' thought and the holiday banter are authorised, and the clipped dialogue survives.
The 'plausibly helpful' Sir James is weakened because his praise of Tommy and his weighed opinion that Tuppence lives are cut. The Julius/Sir James dual-suspect structure still holds.
All four dependencies have both endpoints present in the revised partners. The Charing Cross link is somewhat weaker, as noted in F4.

strengths: All eight verbatim units survive exactly, including V3's italicised reason for the envelope and V7's gentle insinuation.
The closing beat (the note, the peculiar smile, the waste-paper basket, 'The darned fool!') is preserved without comment, so the Julius suspicion holds.
Carter's portrait of Tommy and Tuppence keeps 'He hasn't got any--so he's difficult to deceive' and 'Pace and stamina' in his clipped register.
No line implies that Carter or the PM suspects Sir James, and the 'Inspector Brown' interjection and 'my case' exit stay suggestively unexplained.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's frame and all eight verbatim lines. These include Tommy's letter, the sealed envelope and its midnight-on-the-28th deadline, 'Pace and stamina', the 'shadow behind', the telegram text, 'Perhaps it never left it', and Julius's unexplained smile. The misleading suspicion of Julius survives, and nothing reveals Sir James. Several of the revision's trims remove small connective links, though. These are Carter's reason for refusing to open the envelope, Sir James's request for information on the New York body, Sir James's helpful-seeming reasoning about Tuppence being alive, and the 'took it for granted he had made a mistake' explanation of the Charing Cross clue. The letter's hedges and the irony around Sir James are also thinner. None is a blocker, but several are cheap to restore.
